facts_and_myths.claim: The groundbreaking 1933 King Kong stop-motion model was only about 18 inches (45 centimeters) tall.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Special effects pioneer Willis O'Brien animated a steel armature covered in foam rubber and rabbit fur frame-by-frame on miniature tabletop sets.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Multiple small models were built for different stunts.

facts_and_myths.claim: King Kong was an alien who landed on Earth in a prehistoric meteorite.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kong was an ancient surviving species of colossal prehistoric ape native to the isolated ecosystem of Skull Island.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The final line of the 1933 film is: 'It wasn't the airplanes. It was Beauty killed the Beast.'

name: The Starry Night
visual_anchor: A hypnotic swirling nocturnal oil painting with a luminous golden crescent moon, glowing stars, and dark cypress tree over a sleeping village.
core_traits: Post-Impressionist masterpiece oil painting created by Dutch master Vincent van Gogh in June 1889
Depicts the view from his east-facing asylum room window at Saint-Remy-de-Provence just before sunrise
Features dramatic swirling cobalt blue sky, eleven glowing golden stars, and a stylized cypress tree
Permanently housed in the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York City since 1941

facts_and_myths.claim: Van Gogh painted The Starry Night while staying as a voluntary patient at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole lunatic asylum.
facts_and_myths.explanation: He checked himself in after severing part of his left ear; the asylum gave him an extra ground-floor room to use as a painting studio.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: He viewed the scene from his barred window at 4 AM and painted it from memory during the day.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Starry Night was sold for millions of dollars during Van Gogh lifetime.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Van Gogh sold only one or two confirmed paintings during his impoverished lifetime (The Red Vineyard); The Starry Night gained global renown only after his death.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Physicists have shown the swirling brushstrokes match the mathematical principles of turbulent fluid dynamics.

name: The Last Supper
visual_anchor: A monumental Renaissance mural depicting Jesus Christ and the twelve apostles reacting in emotional shock to a prophesied betrayal.
core_traits: Masterpiece late 15th-century mural painting by Italian Renaissance polymath Leonardo da Vinci
Covers the refectory dining hall wall of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Italy
Depicts the dramatic psychological moment Christ announces one of his twelve disciples will betray him
Renowned for pioneering linear perspective converging on Christ's right temple

facts_and_myths.claim: Leonardo used experimental tempera and oil paint on dry plaster instead of true wet fresco, causing rapid decay.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Leonardo painted slowly, he rejected true wet buon fresco; within just 20 years of completion, the paint began flaking off the damp wall.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It has undergone over five centuries of meticulous restoration to survive.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Last Supper mural was completely destroyed by Allied bombing in World War II.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Allied bombs blew off the roof and side walls of the refectory in August 1943, but sandbags and wooden scaffolding miraculously preserved the mural wall intact.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Leonardo used real citizens of Milan as models for the disciples' faces.

name: The Scream
visual_anchor: An agonizing, alienated figure holding its head with mouth agape in an iconic scream beneath a fiery blood-orange fjord sunset.
core_traits: Iconic Expressionist composition created by Norwegian artist Edvard Munch in 1893
Depicts an agonizing figure with gaunt skull-like face holding its ears beneath a swirling blood-red sky
Symbol of universal human existential angst and psychological anxiety in modern life
Displayed at the National Museum and Munch Museum in Oslo, Norway

facts_and_myths.claim: Munch was inspired by the sunset after an evening walk when he felt an 'infinite scream passing through nature'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Munch wrote in his diary: 'The sky suddenly turned blood-red... I sensed an infinite scream passing through nature.'
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Atmospheric scientists suggest the fiery sunset was caused by volcanic aerosol dust from the 1883 Krakatoa eruption.

facts_and_myths.claim: The central figure is screaming loudly to terrorize passerby pedestrians.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The figure is not making the scream; it is holding its hands over its ears in terror to block out the overwhelming psychic scream of nature.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Versions of The Scream were stolen from Oslo museums in 1994 and 2004, but both were successfully recovered.

name: Girl with a Pearl Earring
visual_anchor: An exquisite oil portrait of a European girl wearing an oriental blue-and-gold turban and an enormous luminous teardrop pearl earring.
core_traits: Dutch Golden Age masterpiece oil painting by Johannes Vermeer painted around 1665
Permanently exhibited at the Mauritshuis art museum in The Hague, Netherlands
Features a young woman turning toward the viewer against a dark background, lips parted
Adorned with an exotic blue-and-yellow turban and an oversized, gleaming pearl teardrop earring

facts_and_myths.claim: The painting is not a formal portrait, but a 'tronie' (a Dutch study of an idealized fictional facial type).
facts_and_myths.explanation: Vermeer was not painting a specific commissioned wealthy noblewoman, but rather an idealized character in oriental costume.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It is widely nicknamed 'The Mona Lisa of the North'.

facts_and_myths.claim: The giant earring is confirmed by jewelers to be made of real solid oyster pearl.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At that massive size, a natural pearl would have been astronomically expensive; researchers believe it was imitation varnished glass or tin.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The blue turban pigment was made from precious lapis lazuli stone imported from Afghanistan.

name: The Thinker
visual_anchor: A monumental bronze sculpture of a nude muscular heroic man resting his chin thoughtfully on the back of his right hand.
core_traits: Masterpiece bronze sculpture created by French sculptor Auguste Rodin in 1904
Depicts a heroic, muscular nude male figure resting his chin thoughtfully upon his right hand
Universal global cultural symbol of deep philosophical contemplation, intellect, and creativity
Originally conceived as the central figure of Rodin's monumental bronze portal 'The Gates of Hell'

facts_and_myths.claim: Rodin originally designed the sculpture to represent Italian poet Dante Alighieri contemplating his Inferno.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Titled originally 'The Poet', the figure was placed at the top of The Gates of Hell contemplating sinners below before Rodin enlarged it as a standalone monument.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: There are over 25 authorized full-size bronze casts exhibited in museums worldwide.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Thinker is carved from a single block of Carrara marble.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The original masterpiece is a cast bronze sculpture, though Rodin's studio also carved marble replicas.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rodin himself is buried beneath a cast of The Thinker at his estate in Meudon, France.
